issue.title: library: a skill's own CLI writing its state file into the folder (browser-skill's .bsk.lock) reads as changed here
issue.body:
## What is wrong

`browser-skill` (tencent/browserskill, installed from `crates/bsk-cli/skill`) ships a CLI, `bsk`, that keeps a daemon. Every time that daemon starts — and on `bsk doctor` — each folder it finds a skill installed in gets an empty `.bsk.lock` written into it. The library's folder is one of them, through the link magpie makes (`~/.claude/skills/browser-skill` → `~/.config/magpie/library/skills/browser-skill`).

`hashFiles`/`hashWalk` count that file, so the folder's hash no longer equals `Skill.Hash`. The Library page says the skill was changed here, `magpie library skill update browser-skill` refuses with `EditedError`, and an update of every skill leaves this one as it is. Nothing was edited. Deleting the file lasts only until the daemon starts again.

The copies fare the same: `~/.cursor/skills/browser-skill` and `~/.pi/agent/skills/browser-skill` each hold their own `.bsk.lock`, and the same `Changed` path reads them as edited.

## Steps

1. Install tencent/browserskill's skill from GitHub into the library.
2. Run `bsk` once — its daemon starting is enough.
3. Open the Library page: the skill says it was changed here. Run `bsk doctor`, read it again: still.

Reproduced on Windows 11 with magpie 0.1.2920 and bsk 0.4.1. Nothing here is Windows-specific: any CLI that keeps its state in the folder its skill lives in does the same.

## Where

`skipInSkill` (`internal/library/skill_edits.go`) leaves aside the library's mark, `.git` and `.DS_Store`; #1072 would widen it to `desktop.ini` and `Thumbs.db` for every walker. A tool's own state file is the same kind of thing — not the skill's bytes — but unlike a file manager's, it can be named in advance.

## What could change

- Put `.bsk.lock` in that list beside `desktop.ini`. One line, and #1072's shape already carries the list to hashing, comparison, copying and carried bundles. It names one tool's file, and there will be more of them.
- Or leave aside what a skill's folder gains that no walker should carry anyway — `*.lock`, or empty dotfiles written after the fetch. Wider, and it can hide a real edit, so probably not.
- bsk could stop writing inside a folder it didn't install, but it doesn't recognise the library's link as its own (`untracked installation differs from the bundled skill`), so it has nowhere else to keep the mark.

The first is the one I'd ask for. The general list is a decision for you to make, not me to assume.

comments.body:
A fix is on [the fork branch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5240-ignore-browser-skill-runtime-lock), commit [7cd33dec4](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/7cd33dec457d8bc8f57d92071b854989b6580217), based on `ed0ab567`.

The exact `.bsk.lock` runtime mark is excluded from skill hashes, edit tracking, mirrors, copies and carried bundles. Other lock files remain skill content; real edits still prevent an update. The existing `.DS_Store` hash modes are unchanged.

Filesystem regressions using linked and copied skill installs reproduce the false edit/update refusal on the base and pass with the fix; they also check real edits, ordinary locks, copying and bundles. Full library tests and the focused parent checks passed under `-race`; library vet, formatting and full `nogui` build passed.

A saved hash from an older version that already included `.bsk.lock` can still conservatively report an edit if the mark has since changed or disappeared: the old digest cannot establish what the other content was. Such a directory remains protected rather than overwritten. Cross-device backup copies also omit this runtime mark. Windows runtime and the full repository test suite were not run. AI-assisted implementation and review.
